# Summary

Implemented the timer-based topmost re-assert so hunt-and-peck overlay labels
stay above context menus / dropdowns / tooltips that open **after** the overlay
loads (the continuous-mode case). Plan:
[`20260728-214134_context-menu-topmost-reassert.plan.qmd`](20260728-214134_context-menu-topmost-reassert.plan.qmd).

# What changed

`src/HuntAndPeck/Views/OverlayView.xaml.cs` only:

- Cached the HWND as `_hwnd` at load.
- Extracted `ReassertTopmost()` — `SetWindowPos(HWND_TOPMOST, SWP_NOACTIVATE |
  SWP_NOMOVE | SWP_NOSIZE)`, guarded on `_hwnd != IntPtr.Zero`.
- Replaced the one-shot with a call to `ReassertTopmost()` plus a
  `DispatcherTimer` (`TopmostReassertIntervalMs = 100 ms`) that re-asserts on
  every tick while the overlay is up.
- Added an `OnClosed` override that stops the timer and zeroes the HWND.

No new P/Invoke (all symbols already in `User32.cs`), no `.csproj` change, no
`App.config` knob. Diff: +60 / −3 in `OverlayView.xaml.cs`.

# Why this fixes the context-menu case

Within `ZBID_DESKTOP` (the band application windows live in) the
most-recently-positioned window wins. The old one-shot ran only at load, so a
popup created mid-session landed above the overlay and stayed there. The timer
re-asserts every 100 ms, pushing the overlay back above any same-band popup.
`SWP_NOACTIVATE` means the menu beneath never loses activation, so it stays
open. Labels are click-through, so a menu visible beneath a floating label is
still clickable via synthesized absolute-coordinate clicks.

# Non-goal (unchanged)

Toast notifications remain unreachable — they live in
`ZBID_IMMERSIVE_NOTIFICATION`, above all `ZBID_DESKTOP` app windows; no app
window (topmost / admin / UIAccess) can cover them. Suppress via Focus Assist /
Do Not Disturb.
